c. A description of how either the Class A or Class B pathogen reduction requirements are met,
          or whether sewage sludge placed on a surface disposal site is covered with soil or other
          material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Class A vs Class B pathogen reduction applies, or whether daily cover is the operative requirement, changes which monitoring/reporting obligations are in force and how absent pathogen-reduction evidence should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: d. A description of how the vector attraction reduction requirements are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which vector-attraction reduction method is required affects whether associated monitoring or descriptive reporting is obligatory and how missing related evidence is categorized.

candidates.exact_span:
e. Results of a groundwater monitoring program developed by a qualified ground-water
          scientist, or a certification by a qualified groundwater scientist may be used to demonstrate
          that sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit does not contaminate an aquifer.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The disjunctive allowance of monitoring results versus certification changes which evidence type is required, whether numeric groundwater results must be compared to limits, and whether missing monitoring can be treated as a documented alternative compliance path.

candidates.exact_span: a. Report No for no liner and leachate collection system at surface disposal site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a surface disposal site lacks a liner and leachate collection system determines which permit section and pollutant-limit regime apply, which annual DMR items are required, and how to interpret absent data for sites that may fall under a different requirement set.

candidates.exact_span: b. The frequency of monitoring listed in Element II, Section I.D. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable monitoring frequency is incorporated by cross-reference; different readings of which Element II, Section I.D. frequency applies change expected monitoring intervals and whether a missing result reflects a required unsatisfied obligation or a non-required period.

candidates.exact_span: c. Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) results (Pass/Fail).
candidates.computation_change_reason: TCLP Pass/Fail is an enforceable numeric-style compliance criterion that must be reported; interpretation of applicability and pass/fail threshold affects limit comparison and monitoring obligation rows.

candidates.exact_span:
d. The concentration (mg/K g) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 5 as well as the
          applicable pollutant concentration criteria listed in Table 5.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Table 5 pollutant concentrations and criteria define the numeric limits to compare against reported sludge measurements and establish which parameters must be monitored and reported annually.

candidates.exact_span: e. The concentration (mg/Kg) of PCB's in the sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: PCB concentration reporting establishes a monitored parameter whose applicable numeric limit and exceedance determination depend on how the requirement and any referenced criteria are interpreted.

candidates.exact_span:
g. Level of pathogen reduction achieved (C lass A or Class B), unless Vector attraction
          reduction alternative no. 11 is utilized.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The exception for vector attraction reduction alternative no. 11 conditionally removes the pathogen-reduction reporting requirement; different interpretations of whether that alternative is utilized change required monitoring and whether absent pathogen data is documented non-requirement versus missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span:
h. List Alternative used as listed in Section I.C.3.(a. or b.). Alternatives describe how the

candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Section I.C.3 alternative applies determines the operative pathogen-reduction compliance pathway and whether associated reporting is required or excused, affecting monitoring-obligation and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: i. Vector attraction reduction Alternative used as listed in Section I.C.4.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The selected Section I.C.4 vector-attraction alternative—including whether alternative no. 11 is used—changes which monitoring and annual reporting items are required and how missing vector-attraction evidence is interpreted.

candidates.exact_span:
n. The certification statement listed in 503.27(a)(1)(ii) or 503.27(a)(2)(ii) as applicable to the
          permittees sludge disposal activities, shall be attached to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which 503.27 certification variant applies, and whether it is attached, affects whether missing numeric results can be treated as a documented no-data/compliance state versus inadequate evidence of required monitoring.

For surface disposal sites with a liner and leachate collection system, pollutant limits are expressly none; whether a site qualifies under Section III changes whether any numeric pollutant limit applies for comparison.
